en: The Sūtra on the Severing of Fever Spoken by the Buddha.
At that time, the Buddha was in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly. Ānanda, his body frail and weak, joined his palms and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, in that world of Jambudvīpa to the south, there has suddenly arisen a celestial fever of such fierce and violent miasma."
"It is like a fierce fire spreading uncontrollably, and countless people have died. How can they be saved? The Buddha told Ānanda, "Listen attentively;
I shall explain this for you. This disease is caused by spirits who constantly spit out foul poisons to harm the people."
When first afflicted by illness, there is headache and alternating chills and fever; all one hundred joints ache with intense, piercing pain. Ānanda said:
"If there are sons or daughters of good family who can know the names of the seven demons and pay them reverence, will this illness be removed?
For you, I shall now speak the incantation for removing illness, which says: [Insert incantation here]
Homage to the Buddha. Homage to the Dharma. Homage to the Saṃgha. Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara. Svāhā! May pestilence be eliminated!
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions, the great Bodhisattvas, and all the noble Sangha of sages heard me recite this Vajra...
Regarding the secret mantras, he also spoke of the names of the seven spirits:
the spirit of many nightmares, the spirit Akhani, the spirit Nikhasi, the spirit Agana, the spirit Parani, the spirit Abira, and the spirit Badhri.
"You all should know: this deity is named 'Swift Departure through Mindfulness. He will not dare to cause harm, and the poisonous vapors affecting that person will be entirely dissipated.
They shall obtain the protection of Vajrapāṇi, their bodies will be peaceful and joyful, and they will be free from all calamities."

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, and the entire great assembly were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it.
Thus ends the *Sutra on Severing Warmth* preached by the Buddha.
